subject: POC alignment: evaluation goals, timelines & ownership (next steps)
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@bluefield.ai>, Tom Gallagher <tom.gallagher@bluefield.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC alignment: evaluation goals, timelines & ownership (next steps)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Below is a compact recap + proposed next steps so we can get the POC kicked off without ambiguity. I pulled the timeline and ownership into the attached POC evaluation template ("poc-eval-template.xlsx").

Recap (from our discussion)
- Objective: Validate latency and cost per inference on your anonymized sample of query logs (~20k requests/day) and confirm integration pattern for real-time scoring at 95th percentile SLA.
- Success criteria (customer-defined):
  - 95th percentile latency < 120ms for the canonical query at 512 tokens
  - Average cost per call <= $0.009 at production batch profile
  - End-to-end integration test passing with no PII leakage and logging to your SIEM

Proposed POC runbook (2-week timebox)
1) Week 0 (Prep) — data access, wire-up, SOC2/contract checklist
   - Action: BlueField to share a sanitized 48-hour sample stream (S3 link) and confirm network egress policy
   - Owner: BlueField (Elena / Priya)
2) Week 1 (Deploy & Baseline) — private trial deployment in our dedicated trial VPC
   - Action: Redwood provisions trial Dedicated slice, deploy chosen model, run baseline tests
   - Owner: Redwood (Avery + Engineering on-call: Karthik)
3) Week 2 (Validations & Handover) — run joint load tests, collect latency/cost, and hand off monitoring hooks
   - Action: Share RACI, final report, and plan for production rollout if criteria met
   - Owner: Joint (Marissa to own report delivery)

Key owners (preliminary RACI)
- Technical lead / infra: BlueField infra (Tom) — responsible for sample data and network rules
- Redwood infra & deployment: Redwood (Avery / Karthik) — responsible for provision, scaling, and runtime params
- App integration / API contract: BlueField app (Priya) — accountable for endpoint wiring and acceptance tests
- Security / compliance signoff: BlueField SecOps (Elena) — consult with Redwood for SOC2 artifacts
- Procurement / contract: BlueField legal/procurement — inform Redwood of any contract gating items

Open questions we flagged
- Will sample data include embedded identifiers that require additional anonymization? (Elena confirms)
- Do you need a non-production IP allowlist or full VPC peering?
- For acceptance testing, do you have an automated smoke test harness we can trigger?

Attachments: I attached the POC evaluation template + a short SOC2 highlights PDF. Please review and update the "Owners" column in the spreadsheet so we can lock responsibilities.

Next steps
- Elena: share sample S3 link + any network constraints by EOD Fri (06/11)
- Priya: confirm who on your side will run the acceptance harness (name + contact)
- Marissa: draft MOU + mutual action plan for procurement (shared by 06/09)
- Avery/Karthik: provision trial slice and send connection details by 06/10

I will follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-minute kick-off on Monday (06/14) if the prep items land on time.

Thanks —
Avery
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: POC alignment: evaluation goals, timelines & ownership (next steps)

Hi Avery —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Data & anonymization: The sample will be a sanitized export (we will remove direct PII) but it will still contain hashed IDs and timestamps. We will share a short schema doc along with the S3 link.
2) Network: We’d prefer an allowlisted IP for the short trial (no peering unless we hit production). I’ll have Tom provide the IP range by EOD Friday.
3) Acceptance harness: We have a lightweight smoke harness that our QA team owns. Priya will be the contact and can run it once you provide endpoint details.

On ownership — suggest a small tweak to the RACI to reflect that BlueField App (Priya) is also responsible for acceptance test definition (not just execution).

We can confirm the S3 link by Friday. We also need Redwood to share any SOC2 artefacts beyond the summary for our procurement review — do you have an audit report or an SOC2 letter we can share internally?

Thanks,
Elena
